prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: O=C1Nc2ccc(Cl)cc2[C@@](C#CC2CC2)(C(F)(F)F)O1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL247

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibitory concentration for 50% inhibition of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitory activity against Wild Type Reverse transcriptase using (poly)rC600*(oligo)dGT as template primer.
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
INSUFFICIENT_INFO is not a valid response. You must commit to COMMENSURABLE or NOT_COMMENSURABLE.
If you lack direct evidence, make your best guess based on compound structure and target identity.
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.72, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 against wild-type HIV-1 reverse transcriptase in a biochemical format with high confidence scores, and while Assay B specifies the template-primer used, standard RT inhibition assays for NNRTIs like this efavirenz analog typically yield comparable IC50 values across similar biochemical setups."}
